title: The dwelling (Exodus 35–40)
hookLine: everyone brings something, and the cloud fills the tent

lines: PLEASE STOP. WE HAVE TOO MUCH.
cards: Here's a sentence you'll almost never hear in a parish bulletin: please stop giving, we have too much. It's in Exodus.
Moses asks for materials for a tent where God will dwell among the people, and only from those whose hearts move them to give.
They come morning after morning with gold jewelry, colored yarn, goat hair, wood, oil and spices, until the craftsmen tell Moses the people are bringing much more than they need.
So Moses sends word through the camp: nobody make anything else for the sanctuary. The people had to be held back from giving.

teach.b: First, the gifts. The last six chapters of Exodus read like a building inventory, and that's the point: everyone's in it. Rulers bring precious stones.

Skilled women spin blue, purple and scarlet yarn with their own hands, and some spin goat hair. Others bring their bronze mirrors, which are melted down for the great washbasin. Nobody's gift is too ordinary.

God calls a craftsman named Bezalel and fills him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, understanding and skill, to work gold, cut stones, carve wood. What the Spirit gives him, the text says, is skill with his hands.
A partner named Oholiab works with him, and they teach others. Third, the dwelling. In Hebrew it's the mishkan, from a verb that means to dwell or to settle.
It's a tent, made to be taken down and carried.

teach.h: MISHKAN: THE CLOUD FILLS THE TENT.
teach.b: When it's set up, the cloud covers it, and the glory of the Lord fills it so completely that Moses himself can't go in. The God of the burning mountain now lives in a tent in the middle of the camp.
Fourth, where Catholics see it every Sunday.

teach.h: THE TABERNACLE, NAMED FOR THE TENT.
teach.b: The place in a Catholic church where the Eucharist is kept is called the tabernacle, named for this tent, and for Catholics the lamp burning beside it says what the cloud said: God is here.
John's Gospel uses the same picture: the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us. The Greek verb means, literally, he pitched his tent.

how: In Catholic churches the Eucharist is reserved in a tabernacle, named after the tent in Exodus, with a lamp kept burning beside it, and parishes rely on volunteers' skills, from musicians and sacristans to cooks and catechists.

o: the permanent stone temple built in Jerusalem
the house Moses built for his own family
the tent where God's glory lived among his people

games.q: what's inside the dwelling — tap the pairs.
p: filled with the spirit of God for craft

s: Moses had to tell the people to stop giving
the craftsmen said there was more than enough, so Moses sent word through the camp.
only gold and silver were used for the dwelling
goat hair, yarn spun by hand, wood, oil and even mirrors went into it.
Moses walked right into the tent once the cloud filled it
the glory filled it so completely that Moses couldn't go in.

games.q: you're one of the craftsmen. every morning the people bring more gold, yarn and wood. you already have more than the work needs. what happens?
o: you store the extra for later.
you tell Moses, and he tells the people to stop.
games.why: they tell Moses there's too much, and he sends word through the camp: no one make anything more. the people were held back from giving.

practice: Bezalel brought his hands, the women their spinning, someone a mirror: what's yours?
Maybe you cook, fix a sink, keep accounts, sing, drive, read aloud or set up chairs; picture one community you belong to, and the one place that gift would fit.
If you pray, offer that skill to God; if not, simply notice that you have something to bring.

wordCard.voice: The dwelling. The tent built from everyone's gifts, where the cloud of God's glory came to live in the middle of the camp. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: dwelling place, from shakan, to dwell or settle. the tent where God's glory came to rest.

carryVoice: Your line: everyone brought something. Even a mirror ended up in the sanctuary. Day three hundred eighty-one, done.

sources.q: the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us
